messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Cluster us-west-batcher reporting high memory paging and multiple node flaps. Pod continuous-batcher-54 restarted 3x in 2m with OOM / cuda errors. Affected capacity ~ 6 nodes.

maya (oncall): on it. seeing spike in queue length and the accumulator is growing beyond expected. paging started 2m ago. pulling logs now.

devin: quick triage — looks like KV cache prefetched keys kept growing after a missed eviction. batch accumulator didn't age out; continuous-batcher kept accepting new requests until OOM.

ash: do we have a quick throttle we can flip? can we set BATCH_MAX_REQUESTS=32 for the service to cap growth?

maya (oncall): pushing a hotpatch to set BATCH_MAX_REQUESTS=32 on the routing group. will apply to us-west-canary first.

ops-bot: Deploy initiated by maya (oncall) — rolling update continuous-batcher/us-west-canary (image redwood/runtime:v3.14-hotfix)

devin: also enabling kernel-level cgroup oom_kill_disable=false? actually we want kernel OOM to avoid silent paging. check the node-level config.

maya (oncall): runbook step: if paging persists, scale-down non-critical tenants and enable qdisc preemption on nodes. trying BATCH_MAX now.

samir: picking this up for the overnight. can you drop the exact kubectl patch you ran?

maya (oncall): pasted:
```bash
kubectl -n inference patch deployment continuous-batcher -p '{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"containers": [{"name": "batcher","env": [{"name":"BATCH_MAX_REQUESTS","value":"32"}]}}]}}}'
```

maya (oncall): canary applied — traffic routed 10% -> canary. monitoring queue length and resident memory.

devin: logs from the crashing pod (truncated):
```
E 03:21:42 runtime.cpp:412] KVPrefetch: growth to 1.8GB beyond limit
E 03:21:44 cuda_driver.cpp:98] CUDNN_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED at memcpy
E 03:21:44 runtime.cpp:423] Fatal: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
```

ash: ugh, CUDA_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS typically from bad kernel args after memory corruption. but given KV growth, paging likely forced memory remapping and weird addresses.

customer-support: heads-up — two customers in eu-west reported 5-10s latency spikes and some 5xxs. collecting ticket ids.

lina: putting customer update on rotation: "We're investigating a runtime memory growth issue affecting inference latency in us-west; mitigation is in progress. We'll share ETA shortly." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ops-bot: Rollback of redwood/runtime:v3.14-hotfix completed on continuous-batcher/us-west (by maya (oncall)). :white_check_mark:

devin: rollback avoided the new image; but root cause appears algorithmic in accumulator drain code. I can reproduce locally with stress tool using long-running small requests causing unbounded accumulator growth.

maya (oncall): creating a follow-up issue and tagging eng-runtime. assigning to devin + ash for a proper fix. samir — keep watch on throttles and if paging reappears escalate to eng-sre.

samir: acked. i'll keep 15m watch and will scale nodes down if stabilization holds.

devin: notes for the fix: add an age-based eviction to accumulator and defensive checks before prefetch; add metric accumulator_size_bytes and alarm at 1GB. PR incoming.

ash: workaround for now: enable `--prefetch-max-entries=5000` and `--eviction-age-ms=60000` in the config. can be rolled via feature flag per-cluster.

lina: posted customer update: "Mitigation in place; we're throttling new batches and expect normal latency within 10-20 minutes. We'll follow up with root cause and permanent fix." :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident followup ticket created: INF-2026-0473

incident-bot: Incident alert cleared in us-west — error rate returned to baseline. :white_check_mark:

maya (oncall): handoff to samir for monitoring. full RCA will be in the ticket; adding logs and stack traces.

samir: taking over. will ping if anything pops. good work team.

devin: PR 4123 opened with accumulator age eviction + metrics. marking as high priority. request code review from eng-runtime.

lina: adding postmortem note to incidents channel once RCA ready.

customer-support: customers notified; tickets updated. thanks everyone.

ops-bot: Summary: root cause - accumulator age/eviction bug causing unbounded KV prefetch + memory growth -> paging -> CUDA illegal address -> pod restarts. Mitigations - set BATCH_MAX_REQUESTS, enable prefetch limits, rollback image. Owner - eng-runtime (devin). Next steps - metrics + alarm, code fix, postmortem. :spiral_calendar:

samir: confirmed stable at +22m. closing oncall handoff unless further alerts.

maya (oncall): signing off shift. :zzz: Thanks all.
